documents.title: Department of Computer Science Policies for Using Generative AI (GAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs)
documents.summary: The CS department sets a default AI policy for all CS courses and activities. It requires attribution, bans wholesale substitution of student work, and lists acceptable uses. In courses AI is allowed only if the instructor permits it in writing (with UPD approval for undergraduate classes).
documents.stance_why: Although it lists acceptable uses, the course default is "AI may be used in undergraduate classes if and only if the instructor permits it in writing", and AI "may not be used as a wholesale substitute"; so AI is banned unless permitted, which is restrict.

units.why: Scope sentence: the policy "applies to all CS Department courses and academic activities", so it is the department-wide framework (P56); the default-for-silent-syllabi rule is coded separately.
units.anchor: This default policy applies to all CS Department courses and academic activities

units.why: "For any course that does not have a specific policy, this document defines the default AI use policy" states the fallback when a course is silent, so P06 fits.
units.anchor: For any course that does not have a specific policy, this document defines the default
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P06 but A said instructor/before-course and B said all/course-start. The source ("For any course that does not have a specific policy, this document defines the default AI use policy") tells course owners what applies when they set no policy, a policy-design matter, so instructor/before-course. Both coders said informs; kept.

units.why: "This policy largely follows the one published by the Graduate School" describes how the policy was derived, which is P84 (how the policy was made).
units.anchor: This policy largely follows the one published by the Graduate School

units.why: The policy is "designed to protect both instructors and students from potential pitfalls" that lead to "academic integrity/dishonesty violations"; the reason is integrity, so P95 rather than skill-building P41.
units.anchor: designed to protect both instructors and students from potential pitfalls
units.fit_note: Rationale is protection of instructors and students from integrity violations, not explicitly fairness.

units.why: "will be reviewed and updated periodically as the AI field advances" commits to revisiting the policy, so P54.
units.anchor: will be reviewed and updated periodically as the AI field advances

units.why: The department says it takes "no position" on "the challenging problem of detecting the use of AI tools". This is neither relying on detectors (P40) nor declining to police (P60); it only declines to take a position, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: we do not take a position at this time on the challenging problem of detecting
units.uncovered_note: The department explicitly takes no position on detecting AI use, calling it separate from the policy.
units.resolution_why: A coded UNCOVERED, B coded P60. The source says "we do not take a position at this time on the challenging problem of detecting the use of AI tools". That is not a statement that the department will not police AI use (P60) and not reliance on detectors (P40), so UNCOVERED, as A did.

units.why: "AI use must be attributed" is a mandatory disclosure requirement for students, so P24.
units.anchor: AI use must be attributed (e.g., you must cite your sources
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P24, student, during-work, must. B set unit_stance permit; the source "AI use must be attributed" is a requirement, so require (A).

units.why: "AI may not be used as a wholesale substitute for the work expected of students: solution generation, coding, or scholarly writing" bans having AI produce submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: AI may not be used as a wholesale substitute for the work expected of students

units.why: "very limited use in theses and dissertations, and then only if it is integral to the work" governs AI in research writing, so P62.
units.anchor: AI should have very limited use in theses and dissertations
units.resolution_why: Both gave P62 and student/during-work. A said should-not, B said should. The source "AI should have very limited use in theses and dissertations" limits use, so should-not, unit_stance restrict.

units.why: "AI may be used for brainstorming ideas" is a permission for brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: AI may be used for brainstorming ideas

units.why: "for exam preparation" is a separate permitted use (study aid), P14.
units.anchor: for exam preparation
units.policy: AI may be used for exam preparation

units.why: "for finding initial information" lets AI be used like a search engine to learn, P12.
units.anchor: for finding initial information
units.policy: AI may be used for finding initial information
units.fit_note: Permits finding initial information and related papers, not explicitly tutoring on concepts.

units.why: "generating initial lists of ideas and/or related papers to investigate" permits AI for exploring directions; nearest is P15, though it also covers literature leads.
units.anchor: generating initial lists of ideas and/or related papers to investigate
units.policy: AI may be used for generating initial lists of ideas and/or related papers to investigate
units.fit_note: Also covers using AI to find related papers, which P15 does not name.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this clause separately (B folded it into the "finding initial information" unit). The source lists "for generating initial lists of ideas and/or related papers to investigate" as its own permitted use, so it is kept as a separate rule, P15 as nearest type.

units.why: "some image generation" is permitted; no type covers image generation, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: and for some image generation
units.policy: AI may be used for some image generation
units.uncovered_note: AI may be used for some image generation.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The source lists "and for some image generation" as a permitted use; it is a real permission and no existing type covers image generation, so it stays UNCOVERED.

units.why: "AI may be used to polish up some text you have written (e.g., like an advanced spell/syntax checker)" permits editing support, P91.
units.anchor: AI may be used to polish up some text you have written

units.why: "All instructors are encouraged but not required to define their own AI policy" leaves the course rule to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: All instructors are encouraged but not required to define their own AI policy.

units.why: "AI may be used in undergraduate classes if and only if the instructor permits it in writing" makes AI barred unless the instructor allows it; the instructor-decides element is P04 (P06 is the fallback for silent syllabi, not this).
units.anchor: AI may be used in undergraduate classes if and only if the instructor
units.fit_note: Also makes the permission conditional on writing, so the default is restrictive.
units.resolution_why: A coded P04 instructor/before-course/must; B coded P06 student/during-work/must-not. The source "AI may be used in undergraduate classes if and only if the instructor permits it in writing" makes the instructor the gate for allowing AI in a course (P04), and the rule is addressed to instructors who must give written permission, so instructor/before-course/must, unit_stance restrict. P06 (fallback when silent) does not fit because the sentence is the permission requirement, not the fallback.

units.why: "with prior written approval of the Undergraduate Program Director" names who grants exceptions to the default, P80.
units.anchor: with prior written approval of the Undergraduate Program Director (UPD)

units.why: "AI may be used in graduate classes if and only if the instructor permits it in writing" is the graduate analogue, an instructor-set rule (P04).
units.anchor: AI may be used in graduate classes if and only if the instructor permits it
units.resolution_why: Same reasoning as the undergraduate sentence. A coded P04 instructor/before-course/must; B coded P06 student/during-work/must-not. The source "AI may be used in graduate classes if and only if the instructor permits it in writing" is the instructor-permission gate, so P04, instructor, before-course, must, restrict.

units.why: "encouraged (but not required) to discuss any class-specific AI policy with the Graduate Program Director" names a consultative role for the GPD, P80.
units.anchor: discuss any class-specific AI policy with the Graduate Program Director
units.fit_note: Consultation with a named officer rather than interpretation or enforcement.

units.why: "must publish it on their class website, in syllabi, and/or in assignment documents" requires custom AI policies to be communicated, P09.
units.anchor: must publish it on their class website, in syllabi, and/or in assignment documents
units.fit_note: The duty to publish applies only to instructors who define a custom AI policy, not to every syllabus.
units.resolution_why: Both gave P09, instructor, course-start, must. A set unit_stance require, B neutral. The sentence is a publication duty for custom policies and does not itself require or forbid AI use, so neutral.

units.why: "students should be able to stand in front of a class ... and explain their entire solutions and work" requires understanding of all submitted work, P30.
units.anchor: students should be able to stand in front of a class, instructors, and/or TAs
units.resolution_why: Both gave P30, student, during-assessment, should. A set unit_stance neutral, B require. The source says students "should be able to stand in front of a class... and explain their entire solutions", an accountability expectation that does not take a position on AI use, so neutral.

documents.unit: Department of Technology, AI and Society
documents.title: Technology, AI and Society's Policy for Using Generative AI (GAI) & Large Language Models (LLMs)
documents.summary: The DTAS department gives seven default rules: attribute AI use, no wholesale substitution, very limited use in serious work, permitted uses such as brainstorming and polishing, explain your work, and publish the policy. Custom instructor policies need UPD permission for undergraduate courses.
documents.stance_why: The seven general rules ban only using AI "as a wholesale substitute" for student work and limit it in serious academic work, and otherwise say "AI may be used for brainstorming ideas, for exam preparation" and "to polish text you have written", with attribution required. Unlike the CS policy, no rule says AI is banned unless an instructor permits it. AI is allowed with conditions, so permit. Coder A said restrict because of the narrow list of uses; coder B said permit.

units.why: The policy is "Aligned with university-wide guidelines", tying it to existing university guidance, P77.
units.anchor: Aligned with university-wide guidelines
units.fit_note: Alignment with university-wide guidelines rather than a legal-compliance duty. B coded this UNCOVERED: the department policy states it is aligned with the university-wide guidelines.
units.resolution_why: A coded P77, B coded UNCOVERED. The source "Aligned with university-wide guidelines" states that the department policy follows the university-level guidance, which is the nearest fit to P77 (comply with existing university policy), though it states alignment rather than a duty. Kept P77 with a fit_note.

units.why: The sentence gives the purpose: the policy "provides clear guidance to promote responsible use, uphold academic integrity, and prevent ethical issues". That is a rationale grounded mainly in academic integrity (P95) and not the scope statement (P56), which is coded separately.
units.anchor: provides clear guidance to promote responsible use, uphold academic integrity, and prevent ethical issues
units.fit_note: Purpose also includes responsible use and prevention of ethical issues, not only integrity.
units.resolution_why: A coded P56, B coded P95. The sentence gives the purpose of the policy: "provides clear guidance to promote responsible use, uphold academic integrity, and prevent ethical issues". It states why the policy exists (a rationale), not the framework itself, which is the scope sentence coded separately as P56. So P95 with a fit_note.

units.why: "applies to all DTAS academic contexts" states scope, P56.
units.anchor: It applies to all DTAS academic contexts
units.resolution_why: Matches B unit 0 (adoption of the policy for courses, research and academic activities). Both coded P56. A anchored "It applies to all DTAS academic contexts"; either anchor states the scope, A kept.

units.why: "will be updated regularly to reflect technological developments" commits to revision, P54.
units.anchor: will be updated regularly to reflect technological developments

units.why: Cites "AI tools are intended to support—not replace—students' independent reasoning and understanding": a statement of the intended role of AI that keeps students the primary problem-solver (P32). It informs rather than instructs, so actor all and modality informs.
units.anchor: AI tools are intended to support
units.resolution_why: A coded student/should, B coded all/informs. The source "AI tools are intended to support—not replace—students' independent reasoning and understanding" states the purpose of AI tools in the policy, not an instruction to a named actor, so actor all and modality informs (B). P32 and unit_stance restrict kept.

units.why: "The seven general rules are the default DTAS AI policy for courses" gives the fallback when an instructor has no custom policy, P06.
units.anchor: The seven general rules are the default DTAS AI policy for courses
units.fit_note: The rules are a default for all courses with instructors allowed to publish custom policies, rather than a rule for silent syllabi specifically.
units.resolution_why: Both gave P06 and informs. A said instructor/before-course, B said all/course-start. The source "The seven general rules are the default DTAS AI policy for courses and other department work" sets the default that applies to courses; it is a policy-design statement about what applies absent a custom policy, so before-course. Actor kept as instructor, who is the one who may replace it. Fit note merged from B.

units.why: Instructors "who wish to define their own custom AI policy must publish it on their class website, in syllabi" is a communication duty, P09; it also lets instructors set custom rules.
units.anchor: must publish it on their class website, in syllabi, and/or in assignment documents
units.fit_note: The duty to publish applies only to instructors who define a custom AI policy.
units.resolution_why: Both gave P09, instructor, course-start, must. A set unit_stance require, B neutral. It is a publication duty, not a stance on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: "prior permission for an individual policy must be received in writing from the UPD" names who approves exceptions to the default, P80.
units.anchor: prior permission for an individual policy must be received in writing from the UPD

units.why: Graduate instructors "are urged to discuss individual AI policies with the GPD", a consultative step, P80.
units.anchor: urged to discuss individual AI policies with the GPD
units.fit_note: Optional consultation with the GPD rather than an approval or exception process.

units.why: Rule 1: "AI use must be attributed", a mandatory disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: AI use must be attributed
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this separately from the version/prompt details. The source "AI use must be attributed" is the general attribution duty (P24) and the parenthetical about software, version and prompts is a more specific rule (P25) coded in the next unit. Kept as two units.

units.why: The same rule specifies citing "AI software and version and the prompts" and the AI-derived portion, which is P25 (tool, prompt) rather than only P24.
units.anchor: you must cite your AI software and version and the prompts that were used
units.resolution_why: Both gave P25, student, during-work, must. B set unit_stance permit; the source says "you must cite your AI software and version and the prompts that were used", a requirement, so require.

units.why: Rule 2 bars AI as "a wholesale substitute for the work expected to be that of students: homework solutions, paper summaries, or major course writing", P19.
units.anchor: AI may not be used as a wholesale substitute for the work expected

units.why: Rule 3: "very limited use in serious academic work (papers, theses, and dissertations)" is research/scholarship writing, P62.
units.anchor: AI should have very limited use in serious academic work
units.resolution_why: Both gave P62 and student/during-work. A said should-not, B said should. "AI should have very limited use in serious academic work" limits use, so should-not, restrict.

units.why: Rule 4 permits "brainstorming ideas", P15.
units.anchor: AI may be used for brainstorming ideas

units.why: "for exam preparation" is a permitted study use, P14.
units.anchor: for exam preparation
units.policy: AI may be used for exam preparation

units.why: "for finding initial information" permits search-like use, P12.
units.anchor: for finding initial information
units.policy: AI may be used for finding initial information
units.fit_note: Permits finding initial information and related papers, not explicitly tutoring on concepts.

units.why: "generating initial lists of ideas and/or related papers to investigate" permits exploring directions, nearest P15.
units.anchor: generating initial lists of ideas and/or related papers to investigate
units.policy: AI may be used for generating initial lists of ideas and/or related papers to investigate
units.fit_note: Also covers using AI to find related papers, which P15 does not name.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this clause separately (B did not code it). The source lists "generating initial lists of ideas and/or related papers to investigate" as its own permitted use, so it is kept as a separate rule, P15 as nearest type.

units.why: "some image generation" is permitted; no type covers it, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: and for some image generation
units.policy: AI may be used for some image generation
units.uncovered_note: AI may be used for some image generation.

units.why: Rule 5 permits AI to "polish text you have written (e.g., like an advanced spell/syntax checker)", P91.
units.anchor: AI may be used to polish text you have written

units.why: Rule 6: students must "explain their coursework using their own words" whether AI is used or not, P30.
units.anchor: explain their coursework using their own words
units.resolution_why: Both gave P30, student, during-assessment, should. A set neutral, B require. The rule is an accountability expectation that holds "whether AI is used or not", so neutral.

units.why: Rule 7: "This AI policy must be included in the class website and on the class syllabus", P09.
units.anchor: This AI policy must be included in the class website and on the class syllabus
units.resolution_why: Both gave P09, instructor, course-start, must. A set unit_stance require, B neutral; a duty to place the policy on the syllabus does not itself take a position on AI use, so neutral.

documents.resolution_why: Document stance: A restrict (narrow listed uses), B permit. The default rules open broad conditional use (attribution, no wholesale substitution) and contain no "banned unless permitted" gate, so permit.

notes: Two computing documents (CS, DTAS); the university-layer values statement was screened out (exclude) and not coded. Topic codes are the coders' own short labels because AGENT_BRIEF.md was not found. DTAS stance resolved to permit (coders split restrict/permit). CS and DTAS share nearly identical rules and were coded separately. Only-A units kept: image generation, related-papers list, general attribution (DTAS).
